realWorkerSoak.crashRestart: worker SIGKILLed 300 ms into an in-flight request: the killed window fell back exactly once (never a partial worker artifact), supervisor respawned (pid 9599 -> 9668, restarts=1), and the post-restart request's detection payload was byte-identical (timing-stripped) to the pre-crash baseline

leakVerdict: No memory leak detected in the real worker: 200-request sequential leak curve is flat (slope -28.9 kB/request, RSS oscillating in a 626-710 MB band with no monotonic trend); Node client RSS also flat. Fake-backend slopes (+2-4 kB/req) are stub/harness-side accumulation over tiny absolute values, not the production worker.
defectsFound: None in the worker lifecycle. All D09 hardening held under soak: 1300 fake + 243 real requests, 4 injected crash cycles + 1 real SIGKILL, 8 injected error responses — every failed window fell back exactly once, every subsequent window rode a restarted worker, zero orphans, zero payload drift. The only code change to the worker is the additive pid getter used for RSS sampling and restart forensics.

checks.tests: packages/swing-lab suite: 37/38 files pass (462 tests incl. paddleWorker.test.ts 19/19 with the new pid/restart test). test/oodGateRedTeam.test.ts has 2-3 5s-timeout failures on this box — PREEXISTING/ENVIRONMENTAL: that file and everything it exercises are byte-unchanged from the base branch (git diff vs origin/devin/1787988068-wave-c-integration touches only paddleWorker*, package.json script, and wave-e artifacts); the failing tests synthesize adversarial clips with ffmpeg and exceed the 5s vitest timeout on this CPU, timing out standalone as well.

honestNegatives: All numbers are LINUX-CPU NOT-MAC; nothing here measures Mac/MPS or iPhone behavior.

Real-worker soak used 500 ms stride-3 windows to make 200 sequential requests tractable on CPU (~4 s/request); full-window (200-frame) requests were not soaked at this count — D09/C07 cover those shapes at low counts.

The paddle-lab venv is gitignored and was recreated this session (torch 2.13.0+cpu / transformers 5.16.1, matching D09); HF model weights were re-downloaded, so absolute RSS values may shift with library versions.
Request timeouts were exercised only via the fake backend (silent worker) in the existing unit tests, not against the real model.
